The '''2020 Copa Sudamericana second stage''' was played from 27 October to 5 November 2020.<ref name="calendar_new">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/calendario_2020_version_pos_pandemia_06_07_2020_aprobado_consejo.pdf|title=CALENDÁRIO 2020|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref> A total of 32 teams competed in the second stage to decide the 16 places in the [[2020 Copa Sudamericana final stages|final stages]] of the [[2020 Copa Sudamericana]].<ref name="regulations">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/docs2020/Manual-de-Clubes-Sudamericana-2020-es.pdf|title=Manual de Clubes / Reglamento CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2020|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|language=es}}</ref>

The second stage had been originally scheduled to be played from 19 to 28 May 2020, but was postponed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="calendar">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/calendario_2020_aprobado_consejo_13_06_2019.pdf|title=CALENDÁRIO 2020: CONMEBOL Libertadores - CONMEBOL Sudamericana - RECOPA|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref>

==Draw==
<section begin=Draw />
The draw for the second stage was held on 23 October 2020, 12:00 [[Time in Paraguay|PYT]] ([[UTC−03:00|UTC−3]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/es/se-sortean-los-octavos-de-la-conmebol-libertadores-y-la-segunda-fase-de-la-conmebol-sudamericana|title=Se sortean los Octavos de la CONMEBOL Libertadores y la Segunda Fase de la CONMEBOL Sudamericana|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=12 October 2020|language=es}}</ref> For the second stage, the teams were allocated to two pots according to their previous results in this season:<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/es/los-32-clasificados-la-segunda-fase|title=Los 32 clasificados a la Segunda Fase|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=23 October 2020|language=es}}</ref>
*'''Pot 1:''' 10 teams transferred from the Copa Libertadores and six best winners of the first stage from the Copa Sudamericana
*'''Pot 2:''' 16 remaining winners of the first stage from the Copa Sudamericana
The 32 teams were drawn into 16 ties (O1–O16) between a team from Pot 1 and a team from Pot 2, with the teams from Pot 1 hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association could be drawn into the same tie.<section end=Draw />
<section begin=Qualified teams />
The following are the 10 teams transferred from the [[2020 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] (two [[2020 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages#Copa Sudamericana qualification|best teams]] eliminated in the [[2020 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages#Third stage|third stage]] of [[2020 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages|qualifying]] and eight third-placed teams in the [[2020 Copa Libertadores group stage|group stage]]).

==Format==
<section begin=Format />
In the second stage, each tie was played on a home-and-away [[two-legged tie|two-legged]] basis. If tied on aggregate, the [[away goals rule]] was used. If still tied, [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] was not played, and a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] was used to determine the winner (Regulations Article 2.4.2).<ref name="regulations"/>

The 16 winners of the second stage advanced to the [[2020 Copa Sudamericana final stages#Round of 16|round of 16]] of the [[2020 Copa Sudamericana final stages|final stages]].<section end=Format />

==Matches==
The first legs were played on 27–29 October, and the second legs were played on 3–5 November 2020.<ref name="fixture">{{cite web|url=https://conmebol.com/es/emparejamientos-del-camino-hacia-la-gran-conquista|title=Programación de partidos de la Segunda Fase|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=23 October 2020|language=es}}</ref><ref name="fixture_pdf">{{cite web|url=http://conmebol.com/sites/default/files/fixture_sudamericana_segunda_fase_23_10_2020_version_2.pdf|title=PROGRAMA DE PARTIDOS - SEGUNDA FASE|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=23 October 2020|language=es}}</ref>
